- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.5) and prices are falling, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to avoid missing sharp rebounds.  
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); apply a “cool-down” rule: cap forecast at 10% below peak for 3–7 days post-spike.  
- If sentiment swings sharply (e.g., +1.0 to -1.0 in 2–3 days), model often fails to adjust horizon; apply a “sentiment lag” correction: reduce forecast by 2–5% for 1–3 days after sentiment reversal.  
- Mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is > 10% above recent 18d average, reduce by 1–2% per day for 5–7 days; if below, increase by 1–2% per day for 5–7 days.  
- For 30d horizon, model often misses 1–2 day “tail” corrections; add 1–2% buffer to forecast if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
